title: Author Go tests for ProjHub Flask-style boundary, response-shaping, delegated access, unsafe input, and regression behavior

ground_truth_issues.description: A test chain proves a standard participant cannot enumerate, retrieve, mutate, or destroy resources that belong to a different team boundary, while an equivalent same-boundary project/task flow still succeeds.

A test chain proves non-privileged callers do not receive privileged project metadata or internal task/collaboration content through primary responses or secondary packaging flows; seeded marker values must remain absent, while privileged callers retain their broader view.

A test chain proves delegated/share access remains confined to the explicitly granted project, cannot be replayed or stretched to neighbouring resources, and fails once the delegated state is invalid, expired, or incomplete.

A test chain proves diagnostic, legacy, historical, or operational surfaces cannot be used by non-privileged callers to retrieve broad application state, credentials, configuration, or organisation-wide records, while intended privileged access still works.

A table-driven test chain proves crafted inputs across discovery, reporting, outbound-request, and file-retrieval surfaces cannot exfiltrate hidden data or trigger unsafe behaviour, while benign variants on those same surfaces still work.

A test chain proves a non-privileged caller cannot overwrite ownership, boundary placement, or privileged attributes through ordinary project/task update paths, and confirms authoritative state with follow-up reads from more than one surface.
A test verifies delegated-access tokens and shareable links are unique, non-derivable from stable identifiers, and not reused across repeated issuances or different actors.

A test verifies shared, audit, private, archived, or otherwise non-default visibility modes do not leak into unrelated callers' list, discovery, or packaged views, while intended audiences still retain access.

A test verifies non-privileged callers cannot recover internal comments or restricted attachment content through collaboration views, file retrieval, package views, or alternate parent-child lookup paths.
A test verifies rollup, summary, audit-log, or widening-style surfaces do not expand a caller's visibility to organisation-wide figures, internal metrics, or other teams' history.
A test verifies specialised roles such as lead, auditor, or guest remain confined to their documented visibility slice and do not become general cross-team readers.
A test chain triggers malformed or failing requests and verifies error responses do not expose internal runtime details, filesystem hints, stack traces, or executable command text.

Anti-overblock tests prove legitimate privileged and same-boundary flows remain available after fixes, including broader administrative visibility, same-team project actions, and ordinary participant task management.
Tests isolate state with fresh setup or stable seeded markers so results are repeatable and not order-dependent.
Tests use body-level assertions with unique sentinel markers, captured IDs, and reusable helpers, rather than relying only on status codes, exception-only checks, or broad truthiness.
